steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 loaf pans.

Combine flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, nutmeg, allspice, cloves, and salt in a large bowl. Whisk pumpkin, eggs, water, vegetable oil, and vanilla together in a separate bowl. Whisk pumpkin mixture into flour mixture until everything is well mixed: fold in walnuts. Divide batter between the 2 prepared loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is golden and springs back when lightly pressed, 50 to 60 minutes. Cool for 20 minutes before removing from the pans.

raw_recipe.headline: Samhain Pumpkin Bread
raw_recipe.description: This super-moist Samhain pumpkin bread recipe blends warming spices—cloves, nutmeg, and cinnamon—with canned pumpkin for rich, fall-forward flavors.
raw_recipe.name: Samhain Pumpkin Bread

review.reviewBody: In case you're wondering, Samhain (pronounced Sow-en) is a high holiday for Pagans and is known as Halloween to most everyone. As for the recipe, it rocks! Very moist and just really flavorful; I didn't have to tweak it at all. I took it to a potluck celebration and it went over very well. Thanks!

Tried this last night. Doubled the recipe because we had that much pumpkin. Out of allspice, so used a little extra cinnamon and clove, added a dash of ginger. The bread took longer to cook than 60 minutes. One reviewer said in a 9x13 pan they turned out like brownies. There is nothing brownie like about them. The muffins went to work, and disappeared. I had no problem with it rising. Definitely going to make this again.

I loved that this didn't pour on the oil. Only had half the amount of nutmeg so added a smidge more allspice. To make for easier carb counting (diabetic in the family) I made this into 18 muffins @ about 1/4 cup batter per muffin and approximately 29 carbs (rounded up to the nearest carb), set the timer for 18-20 minutes and used the toothpick test. Love the spice mix as I am usually having to add extra spices to pumpkin bread recipies. Burned my fingertips sampling the too hot muffins and before it was done steaming, the flavor was amazing. This will be my go-to recipe for quick pumpkin muffins. Can't wait to make as loaves when I have more time available to bake!

I followed the recipe except that I used pecans instead of walnuts, added about 1/3 cup of chocolate chips, and baked in one large pan. It took 62 minutes. It came out nice and moist, and I liked the level of sweetness (not overly sweet). But there is just something missing in the taste that I couldn't put my finger on. If I make it again I'll try Kefir or Buttermilk or even some yogurt in place of the water to see if that helps.

Tastes wonderful and filled my apartment with the most mouth-watering aroma! I added a 1/2 cup of pecans to the recipe and poured the batter into muffin tins instead of loaf pans. Cooked them for about 20 minutes. It came out great! 
10/10 would cook again

I made a few small changes, just to make it a little healthier. I used whole wheat white flour, cut the sugar by half, used homemade organic pumpkin mash, brewed/cooled chai tea instead of water and melted butter instead of oil. (Low on oil right now.) At the last minute, I added one cup of Hershey's cinnamon chips. I got 18 muffins out of one recipe, medium sized. 350* for 18 minutes was just right baking time. The flavor of these muffins is wonderful, made even better by the addition of cinnamon chips. And the smell while baking? Amazing.

I was dog sitting at a friend's house and didn't have all purpose flour or vegetable oil, so I substituted with whole wheat flour (25% less than all purpose, so about 1 1/3 c) and 1/4 c applesauce. I added raisins instead of walnuts. I was very pleased with the results, except that I should have used smaller loaf pans.

Perfect! I made this at the last minute for a Halloween party. In hopes of cutting down on cooking time and making it easier to serve, i baked in a 9X13 pan. They came out like pumpkin brownies. No major changes...omitted clove, used baking powder instead of soda, flour was half wheat half regular, sugar was half brown half regular. It was gobbled up!

Very yummy! I read the other reviews and substituted brown sugar for 1/2 cup of the white sugar called for. I also used some cranberry juice I had on hand in place of the water in the recipe, and added some dried cranberries to the nuts in the final step. The result was a wonderful sweet dense bread with a touch of tanginess. I didn't really taste the spices as much as I hoped to - next time I'll increase the amounts.

Made a loaf AND 12 muffins/cupcakes. Didn't have allspice; subbed ginger. Didn't have walnuts, subbed toasted pecan pieces. Also added bittersweet chocolate chunks, just 2 ounces so as not to overpower the pumpkin or spices. I DIE! So good.

Love this recipe and followed it almost to a T, I omitted the nuts as I have issues with walnuts. I think I would rather have one loaf in a larger bread pan than two smaller ones since it doesn't rise much. I loved that it didn't require a mixer, only a whisk. It smelled wonderful baking.

Samhain Pumpkin Bread is the absolute best, as there is NO other version or competition to compare this luscious pumpkin bread recipe against. I left out walnuts, since this is completely unnecessary to incorporate into pumpkin bread, and would absolutely ruin it.
i was fine
I made this for a friend who wanted pumpkin bread and she raved about it. It was one of the best ones I’ve made.
Loved it! Making it again this weekend
I absolutely love this recipe. I've been making it for the past 7 years now. It's always amazing. It's apart of my samhain ritual every year.
This recipe is wonderful....I have been making it for last 10 years....
It's perfect the way it is!

Thanks for this recipe, have been cooking this twice already, taste is great and adds positive emotions to Halloween celebration. there is a comment from other person here: "I think she made a mistake in the recipe. There's no baking powder, and as a result all of my bread was flat." - I used only baking soda and everything else according to recipe - bread wasn't flat, it grew, I think, 2.5-3 times comparing to original dough size

I used pecans rather than walnuts. Other than that, made exactly as written. The mold I used held almost the whole batch (which is for two loaves). There was enough left over to make a couple of cupcakes. We all loved it!!
